 Pakistan tax authorities move to operationalise faceless income tax refunds
 Faceless tax refunds launched 
 Pakistan is moving to automate income tax refunds as part of a broader push to reduce delays and limit direct interaction between taxpayers and tax offices. The step follows a presidential order tied to a Rs42.86 million refund claim for tax year 2025 and extends the country’s faceless processing approach beyond customs clearance and assessment.
 Highlights
 President Asif Ali Zardari upheld the introduction of a Faceless Refund Regime for income tax refunds under Section 170A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.
 The new system authorizes automated, application-free, electronic transfers of verified tax credits to taxpayers’ notified bank accounts, aiming to reduce delays and minimize taxpayer-office interaction.
 A pending Rs42.86 million income tax refund claim for tax year 2025 and Islamabad High Court directives accelerate the operationalization of this faceless, automated mechanism within Pakistan's tax administration.
 Presidential order backs automated refund mechanism
As reported by Business Recorder , President Asif Ali Zardari has upheld a decision recommending that the Federal Board of Revenue operationalise a Faceless Refund Regime under Section 170A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The order says refunds tied to tax credits verified through the Board’s computerised system would be sanctioned and transferred electronically into taxpayers’ notified bank accounts without requiring a formal refund application. The President dismissed an FBR representation against an earlier decision in a case involving a pending income tax refund claim of Rs42.86 million for tax year 2025. While doing so, he maintained the recommendation that the Board prescribe an appropriate mechanism for introducing a faceless refund system.
 The decision notes that the FBR has already launched faceless customs clearance and assessment regimes. It adds that the Board should also operationalise the same approach for income tax refunds under Section 170A. Implications for taxpayer services and administration
Tax advisor Khurram Shahzad Butt says the move would reduce delays and improve taxpayer facilitation. He says delayed refunds amount to maladministration and points to the Islamabad High Court’s directions in WP No. 2173/2023 for an automated refund mechanism under Section 170A to minimise taxpayer interaction with tax offices and speed up payments.
 FBR argues that an appeal lies before the Commissioner (Appeals) under Section 170(5) and that the claim remains at the verification stage. Butt says, however, that the appealable nature of a matter cannot shield tax authorities from administrative delay, highlighting the potential for the proposed system to reshape refund processing in Pakistan’s tax administration.
 As we noted earlier, the FBR tax split from January 2027 will separate sales tax and income tax handling.
